answer: A karst registry admits one identity per nullifier. An applicant derives a nullifier from a secret, locks a 75-credit bond to it, and pays a fee. The k-th fee is 15+4(k-1), so the 1,000th fake pays 4,011; 1,000 fakes pay 75,000 in bonds plus 2,013,000 in fees. A prism board publishes a shard letting auditors recompute nullifiers without exposing them. A vine link joins entries sharing a nullifier and burns both bonds. A secret-rental ring fails: a rented secret reused yields one nullifier, so both bonds burn. An honest agent locks 75, refundable after one epoch, plus 15.
